cases.title: An expression of exactly 8192 bytes evaluates
cases.notes: The limit is INCLUSIVE. Whitespace padding keeps the row about length alone: the expression is `1` plus 8191 spaces.

cases.title: 8193 bytes is EXPR_TOO_LONG
cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0001. An implementation using `>=` where the spec says `>` fails 0001; one with no limit fails this row.

cases.title: A two-byte character counts twice: 4095 x U+00E9 in quotes is exactly 8192 bytes and evaluates
cases.notes: 4097 characters, 8192 UTF-8 bytes. Within the limit however it is counted.

cases.title: 4096 x U+00E9 in quotes is 8194 bytes but only 4098 characters: EXPR_TOO_LONG
cases.notes: THE CROSS-LANGUAGE ROW. JavaScript's `.length` counts UTF-16 units, Python's `len` counts code points and PHP's `strlen` counts bytes -- three runtimes, three different numbers for one string. The limit is UTF-8 BYTES in every runtime, and an implementation that used its native length passes this row's string as 4098 and accepts it.

cases.title: 8193 bytes of characters the tokenizer would reject is EXPR_TOO_LONG, not EXPR_SYNTAX
cases.notes: Pins the ORDER: the length check runs before tokenizing, so an oversized input costs O(1) work to refuse rather than a scan. An implementation that tokenized first reports EXPR_SYNTAX at offset 0.

cases.title: 63 nested parentheses around a literal is depth 64 and evaluates
cases.notes: A parenthesised group counts as one level even though it produces no node of its own: the parser recurses through it, and recursion is what the limit bounds.

cases.title: 64 nested parentheses is depth 65: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0101. An implementation that does not count groups (because they leave no node in the tree) accepts this.

cases.title: 4000 nested parentheses (8001 bytes, under the length limit) is EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: THE DEFECT. fancy-expr 0.1.1 parsed this by plain recursion -- roughly nine stack frames per parenthesis. Measured on 2026-10-27: Node threw RangeError (maximum call stack size exceeded) and Python RecursionError; PHP's larger stack happened to hold at 4000 and returned 1. Neither crash is the package's own error type, so a host catching syntax errors to reject bad input at save time crashed instead. The length limit alone does not prevent it: 4000 levels fit in 8001 bytes.

cases.title: 8000 opening parentheses and nothing else is EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: Pins that depth is enforced DURING descent, before the missing `)` is reached. An implementation that only measured the finished tree would have to finish parsing first -- which is the recursion that overflows -- and, if it survived, would report EXPR_SYNTAX.

cases.title: 63 chained `!` on a literal is depth 64 and evaluates
cases.notes: An odd number of negations of true.

cases.title: 64 chained `!` is depth 65: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: Unary operators recurse in the parser and in the evaluator. An implementation that counted only brackets accepts this.

cases.title: 1+1+...+1 with 64 terms is 63 left-nested additions, depth 64, and evaluates
cases.notes: A binary chain is parsed by a LOOP, not by recursion, so it never threatens the parser's stack -- but it builds a left-deep tree, and every evaluator here walks the tree recursively.

cases.title: 65 terms is 64 additions, depth 65: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: An implementation that guarded only its own recursion (brackets, unary, ternary) accepts this, and 0303 is what that costs.

cases.title: 1+1+...+1 with 4000 terms (7999 bytes) is EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: Parses fine with no limit at all -- the chain is a loop -- then overflows while EVALUATING the left-deep tree. Measured on fancy-expr 0.1.1: RangeError in Node, RecursionError in Python, 4000 in PHP. A depth limit that counted only parser recursion would let this through to the evaluator.

cases.title: 64 nested array literals is depth 64 and evaluates
cases.notes: An empty array literal is depth 1; each enclosing literal adds one.

cases.title: 65 nested array literals: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0401.

cases.title: 63 nested object literals around a literal is depth 64 and evaluates
cases.notes: Object values nest exactly as array items do.

cases.title: 64 nested object literals around a literal: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0501.

cases.title: x[x[...x[0]...]] with 63 indexings is depth 64 and evaluates
cases.notes: A computed index is a nested expression, so a path holding one is one level deeper than its deepest index.

cases.title: 64 nested computed indices: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0601.

cases.notes: A right-nested ternary chain -- the `else if` shape -- recurses once per link.

cases.title: 64 chained ternaries: EXPR_TOO_DEEP

input.expression: false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : false ? 0 : 1

cases.notes: The off-by-one partner of 0701.

cases.title: A path of 501 dot-segments is depth 1 and resolves (to null)
cases.notes: Dot-segments are read in a loop and walked in a loop; they nest nothing. An implementation that counted every segment as a level rejects a legitimate deep data path.

cases.title: An array literal of 1000 items is depth 2 and evaluates
cases.notes: Width is bounded by the length limit, not the depth limit. An implementation that counted items rejects this.

cases.title: `!(` repeated 31 times around `true` is depth 63 and evaluates
cases.notes: Each `!(` is two levels: the unary operator and the group.

cases.title: `!(` repeated 32 times is depth 65: EXPR_TOO_DEEP
cases.notes: An implementation that counted either construct but not both passes 0803 and accepts this.

cases.title: A malformed expression within every limit carries EXPR_SYNTAX
cases.notes: Every failure now carries a stable code, not only the new ones, so a host can branch on the code without parsing a message. The message stays human-facing and may change; the code may not.
